_source: AI-researched venue CANDIDATES for Manchester and Cheshire, awaiting review — never directly edited by the research agent. Populated by a daily scheduled research agent (2026-08, at explicit user request: 'fan out some research agents who's goal is to run every day to find and suggest new businesses... they shouldn't go beyond cheshire and manchester just yet'; bumped from ~3-5/day to 10/day at a later explicit request). See .claude/agents/curia-research-daily.md for the full research brief/rules this agent works under (Hard rule 1 chain/fast-food screening, real coordinates only, no duplicates, Do/Drink/Eat coverage balance). The research agent commits straight to master for this file (no PR — this queue has zero effect on the live app, nothing reads it except the review agent and the admin dashboard's Growth Insights context). A second, independent daily agent (.claude/agents/curia-suggestion-review.md) re-verifies each `pending` entry and is the only thing that ever promotes one into the real docs/data/venues.json, behind its own pull request — see that file's own doc comment for why the human checkpoint lives there instead of here. Each entry mirrors docs/data/venues.json's own raw shape (name/district/type/spend/lat/lon/base/bands/reason) exactly, so a reviewed-and-approved entry can be moved into that file with a straight copy-paste, plus review-only fields (suggestedDate, status, researchNotes) that get stripped on promotion. `district` values must be a real existing district id from docs/data/districts.json (manchester/cheshire metros only) UNLESS the entry is itself proposing a brand-new district — see district-suggestions.json for that case instead; a venue suggestion should never invent a district id that doesn't exist anywhere.
_reviewWorkflow: status starts 'pending' on every new entry. The daily curia-suggestion-review agent changes it to 'approved' (then copies the venue fields into docs/data/venues.json and removes the entry here, as part of its own PR) or 'rejected' (left here with researchNotes explaining why, as a record so the same candidate isn't re-suggested later — curia-research-daily checks every entry here regardless of status before suggesting anything new). A human's actual review happens by reading/merging the review agent's PR, not by editing this file directly, though a human reviewer (or a future admin-dashboard screen) can still hand-edit an entry's status here if needed.

suggestions.name: Clark Art
suggestions.reason: Bill Clark's own gallery on Ashley Road since 1999, deep in L.S. Lowry and the northern painters he's written the books on — a private dealer's eye, not a gallery chain's algorithm.
suggestions.researchNotes: REJECTED on independent re-verification 2026-09-03: Clark Art (155 Ashley Road, Hale) closed permanently on 3 October 2024 after 18 years, per Bill Clark's own retirement announcement (reported by Altrincham Today, 'An incredible journey: Clark Art to close after 18 years in Hale village'). The prior research pass's sources (Tripadvisor/Artsy/halebarns.com listings) were stale directory pages that hadn't been updated to reflect the closure. Do not re-suggest — the gallery no longer exists.

suggestions.name: Yang Sing
suggestions.reason: Three floors of a Grade II-listed Princess Street townhouse, family-run since the 1970s — bottomless yum cha that still draws a queue nobody seems to mind.
suggestions.researchNotes: REJECTED on independent re-verification 2026-09-03: Yang Sing (34 Princess Street) has been closed since December 2021/early 2022 (kitchen fire, then a lease dispute) and Yang Sing Limited is now in liquidation per Companies House — it never reopened despite the owner's 2022 hope to reopen by 2023/24. The prior research pass's sources (visitmanchester.com, Hardens, Tripadvisor) were stale listings still showing it as an open, operating restaurant. Do not re-suggest unless it demonstrably reopens under new ownership.

suggestions.name: Blue Lobster
suggestions.reason: Italian seafood on the corner of London Road and Brown Street, sourced directly from Rome — a Franciacorta bar downstairs, the kitchen running until midnight upstairs.
suggestions.researchNotes: REJECTED on independent re-verification 2026-09-03: Blue Lobster (34 London Road, Alderley Edge) closed permanently in December 2017, less than nine months after its April 2017 opening, following a staff-payment dispute with owner Andrea Zecchino (reported by alderleyedge.com and Manchester Confidential at the time). No evidence of any reopening or trading activity was found in the eight years since. The prior research pass's Tripadvisor/Luxury Lifestyle Magazine sources were leftover listings from the 2017 opening, not current confirmation. Do not re-suggest unless it demonstrably reopens under new ownership.

suggestions.name: Fire Station Social Cucina
suggestions.reason: A pizza theatre and wood oven where Gusto used to sit on London Road — hand-rolled pasta, Napoli-style bases, and only one other room anywhere doing the same thing.
suggestions.researchNotes: Verified via thebusinessdesk.com, wilmslow.co.uk/alderleyedge.com and the operator's own site (firestationsocial.co.uk): Fire Station Social Cucina, 75 London Road, Alderley Edge SK9 7DY, opened 10 June 2026 in the former Gusto unit — the second site for this specific concept, after the original in Tarporley. Run by 'Project Social Cucina', the restaurant division of Cheshire Pub Company (a separate entity from the 7-pub Cheshire Cat group already referenced elsewhere in this file) — only 2 sites confirmed under the Fire Station Social Cucina name itself, the same 2-site sibling precedent already used for Cibo/Suburban Green/Smoke Wilmslow/Heddy's/Caramello. Flagged for the reviewer: the parent company's own press describes this as 'expansion', so worth a quick re-check at promotion time that a third site hasn't since appeared. Moderate-high confidence otherwise — real, recently opened, well-covered locally, no closure signals. Re-checked again 2026-09-08 (curia-suggestion-review daily pass) specifically for a rumoured third site: none found — same 2-site status as this note originally recorded, still pending, still in docs/data/pending-review-queue.json for a human call rather than re-decided here. DECIDED 2026-09-08 by direct user instruction, in an interactive session: promoted into venues.json with the new `status: 'coming-soon'` field (added the same day specifically for this case) rather than a flat yes/no — real venue, passes Hard rule 1 on site count today, but its editorial confidence marker stays provisional given the parent's stated expansion plans. See venues.json's own note on the new field.

suggestions.name: Prana
suggestions.reason: Two floors of proper acoustics on Ashley Road from the team behind Stockport's Amp — order the cocktail, but the stage is the reason to stay past nine.
suggestions.researchNotes: Verified via CAMRA (camra.org.uk), whatpub.com and Altrincham Today: Prana, 14-16 Ashley Road, Altrincham WA14 2DW, an independent live-music venue and cocktail bar opened November 2023, run by the same team as Amp in Stockport — a real 2-site sibling pair, not a chain, same precedent as Bramhall/Cheadle Hulme's Mounting Stone/Chiverton Tap pair in this batch. RE-VERIFICATION 2026-09-11 (curia-suggestion-review) found the original researcher's 'CAMRA-listed and actively promoted' claim was incomplete: CAMRA and whatpub.com both actually list Prana as 'Closed Long Term' (last updated 28/05/2024), following a reported 'closing until further notice' Facebook announcement from Altrincham Today around the same date — a real closure signal the original pass missed. However, a new company, PRANA F&B LIMITED, was incorporated 13 September 2024 at the same 14-16 Ashley Road address and remains active per Companies House, and a Food Hygiene Ratings record exists for 'Prana - Altrincham' — both consistent with a reopening or change of hands rather than the site sitting empty, but no direct evidence of current 2025/2026 trading (a recent event listing, an active social post) was found either way. Genuinely conflicting signals rather than a clean pass or fail — left pending here and sent to docs/data/pending-review-queue.json for a human call rather than promoted or rejected outright. RE-CHECKED 2026-09-12 (curia-suggestion-review): Curia Command's pending_review collection had no decision recorded yet; still no direct 2026 trading evidence found either way. Left as-is. RE-CHECKED 2026-09-13 (curia-suggestion-review): still no direct 2025/2026 trading evidence either way despite fresh searches (Instagram/Skiddle listings exist for the venue but show no current events; two of this run's source URLs, altrincham.co.uk's own listing and a Skiddle venue page, were blocked by this session's network egress policy and couldn't be checked directly). One new detail surfaced: a Facebook report from around the 2024 closure mentions the owner's intent to convert the venue into an events space, which doesn't resolve whether it's trading today. Curia Command's pending_review collection was empty again this run — no human decision yet. This file previously carried an accidental duplicate of this exact entry (identical content, same 2026-09-11 suggestedDate) — deduplicated down to one today; no information was lost, the surviving entry already carried the fuller, more recently updated research notes. Left pending, unchanged in verdict, same as every prior run since 2026-09-11.

suggestions.name: Nantwich Museum
suggestions.reason: Sixty-odd volunteers on Pillory Street keep the salt town's own story straight — Roman brine pits, the Great Fire, the Civil War siege — free to walk into, and the town's own guided walks start from the same front door.
suggestions.researchNotes: Verified via the museum's own site (nantwichmuseum.org.uk), Nantwich Town Council's own directory and Art Fund: independent, volunteer-run local heritage museum at Pillory Street, Nantwich CW5 5BQ, open Tue-Sat 10am-4pm, free admission, 60+ volunteers, runs its own guided town/riverside walks. Single-site charitable trust, not a chain or franchise — passes Hard rule 1 cleanly, highest-confidence type of candidate (civic/charitable, no commercial footprint to check). Coordinates from doogal.co.uk's postcode geocode for CW5 5BQ (this session's direct postcodes.io/doogal API access was blocked by network egress policy, so the lat/lon was obtained via a web search reporting doogal's own published figure for this exact postcode, not invented). Reuses the existing HERITAGE CENTRE type (Knutsford Heritage Centre, Silk Museum & Paradise Mill) — fits cleanly, no new type needed. Fills Nantwich's most acute gap: the district's only Do-category venue was previously zero (5 venues total, all Eat/Drink) before this addition.

suggestions.name: The Copper Room
suggestions.reason: Amy and Rick Armstrong crowdfunded their way into Charles Roe House's Grade II* rooms — steak and seafood cooked properly, in a silk merchant's own dining room on Chestergate.
suggestions.researchNotes: Verified via the operator's own site (chefrick.co.uk), Macclesfield Nub News (two separate pieces confirming both the Kickstarter-funded opening and the venue name) and Tripadvisor (active listing with 2026-dated reviews): The Copper Room, Charles Roe House, 60-62 Chestergate, Macclesfield SK11 6DY, a fine-dining restaurant and cocktail bar run by chef-owners Amy and Rick Armstrong. No second site or group ownership found anywhere — single-site, independently owned, passes Hard rule 1 cleanly. Coordinates from doogal.co.uk's postcode geocode for SK11 6DY. Reuses the existing FINE DINING type. Fills a real gap: Macclesfield had only 1 Eat-category venue (Chestergate Bistro) against 2 Do and 3 Drink before this addition.

suggestions.name: Plumcake Cafe
suggestions.reason: Cath's own kitchen in the corner of Village Square — a proper cooked breakfast and a pastry counter that doesn't need an afternoon-tea tier to justify itself.
suggestions.researchNotes: Verified via Bramhall Village Square's own tenant directory (bramhallvillagesquare.co.uk), the UK Food Hygiene Ratings register and Tripadvisor: Plumcake Cafe, 11 Village Square, Bramhall SK7 1AW, a family-run breakfast/brunch cafe, single site, no second location found anywhere. Owner Cath has local media profile (appeared on 'Would I Lie to You') but that's a media appearance, not a chain footprint. Passes Hard rule 1 cleanly. Coordinates from doogal.co.uk's postcode geocode for SK7 1AW. Reuses the existing BRUNCH SPOT type (Aldeli, Caramello, Neki). Bramhall was at 7 venues (3 Do, 2 Drink, 2 Eat) before this addition — closes part of its Eat gap.

suggestions.name: The Warren
suggestions.reason: A den of local painters and makers just off Market Place — the Underbanks' answer to a private view that never quite closes its doors.
suggestions.researchNotes: Verified via Stockport Council's own 'Rediscovering the Underbanks' regeneration coverage, the venue's own Facebook page and X account: The Warren, 6 Market Place, Stockport SK1 1EW, an independent local-artist gallery/collective space in the Underbanks regeneration quarter. Single site, no chain footprint found. Passes Hard rule 1 cleanly. Coordinates from doogal.co.uk's postcode geocode for SK1 1EW. Reuses the existing ART GALLERY type. Stockport (Underbanks) was at 7 venues (2 Do, 2 Drink, 3 Eat) before this addition — closes part of its Do gap. Note for reviewer: this is a smaller, less-documented venue than most of this file's gallery entries (no dedicated press coverage found beyond the council's own regeneration round-up and its own social presence) — moderate rather than high confidence, worth a fresh check at promotion time.

suggestions.name: Buon Cibo
suggestions.reason: A family kitchen on Shaw Road doing proper Italian without the tablecloth theatre — the sister site over in Reddish hasn't thinned out what lands on the plate here.
suggestions.researchNotes: Verified via OpenTable (4.5-star, active current bookings), Tripadvisor and the venue's own Instagram/Facebook: Buon Cibo, 17 Shaw Road, Heaton Moor, Stockport SK4 4AG, described as family-run on its own social presence. A second site trading under the same name exists in nearby Reddish (79a-81 Broadstone Road, Stockport SK5 7AS) — both within the same borough, a real 2-site local sibling pair consistent with this file's existing precedent (Cibo/Heddy's/Caramello, Wallop). Owner's name not independently confirmed beyond the 'family run' descriptor both sites use, so flagged as moderate rather than high confidence on the ownership-link specifically, though the chain-footprint check itself (2 sites, same borough, same brand) is solid. Coordinates from doogal.co.uk's postcode geocode for SK4 4AG. Reuses the existing ITALIAN RESTAURANT type. Heaton Moor was at 6 venues (2 Do, 2 Drink, 2 Eat) before this addition, the thinnest district in this run's tally.

suggestions.name: Railway Inn
suggestions.reason: The Davies family's free house by the level crossing, thirty-eight years in — cask ale, a bowling green out back, and none of Mill Lane's usual queue.
suggestions.researchNotes: Verified via CAMRA (camra.org.uk), useyourlocal.com and the pub's own site (railwayinnpub.com): Railway Inn, beside Mobberley station, Mobberley WA16 6LA, a genuine free house (not tied to any brewery) run by the Davies family for 38 years. Deliberately a different pub from every Mobberley venue already in this file (Bull's Head, Church Inn — both Cheshire Cat Pubs & Bars sister pubs; Roebuck Inn, same group, previously researched and deliberately skipped to avoid over-concentrating one seven-pub group in a single small village) — the Railway Inn has no ownership link to that group at all, a genuinely independent alternative. Passes Hard rule 1 cleanly. Coordinates from doogal.co.uk's postcode geocode for WA16 6LA. Reuses the existing COUNTRY PUB type. Mobberley was at 9 venues (3 Do, 2 Drink, 4 Eat) before this addition — closes its Drink gap, the category it had least of.

suggestions.name: Gin Can
suggestions.reason: Kings Court's gin specialist, run by the team behind Cheshire Tap next door — a proper back bar built around one spirit, not a novelty laminated menu.
suggestions.researchNotes: Verified via Altrincham Today (opening coverage naming co-owner Martin Connolly), the venue's own site (gincanaltrincham.co.uk) and Visit Altrincham's business directory: Gin Can, Unit 4, Kings Court, Railway Street, Altrincham WA14 2RD, opened 2019, a specialist gin bar. Co-owned by the same people behind Cheshire Tap, a sister venue in the same Kings Court courtyard — a real, same-complex 2-site sibling pair, not a chain, consistent with this file's existing small-group precedent. Passes Hard rule 1. Coordinates: this session's direct access to postcode-geocoding APIs (postcodes.io, doogal.co.uk) was blocked by network egress policy for this specific postcode (WA14 2RD), so lat/lon was triangulated from two immediately neighbouring WA14 postcodes on the same block (53.384157,-2.35191 and 53.383755,-2.360146) rather than a doogal.co.uk direct hit — real street-level (Railway Street/Kings Court), not a district centroid, but flagged for the reviewer to re-confirm with a direct postcode lookup before promotion. Reuses the existing COCKTAIL BAR type (Gin Can serves a full cocktail list alongside its gin focus) rather than introducing a new type, since no onboarding tile targets gin specifically and Cocktail bars is the closest real fit. Altrincham was at 9 venues (4 Do, 2 Drink, 3 Eat) before this addition — closes its Drink gap, the category it had least of.

suggestions.name: Bench Bistro Bar
suggestions.reason: Small plates and a wine list built for staying past the main course, on Beam Street — the sister site over in Congleton hasn't stretched this kitchen thin.
suggestions.researchNotes: Verified via the venue's own site (benchbistrobar.co.uk), Tripadvisor and findmeglutenfree.com: Bench Bistro Bar, 35 Beam Street, Nantwich CW5 5NA, small plates/wine-led bistro bar. A second site trades under the same name in Congleton (30-34 Lawton Street) — a real 2-town, 2-site sibling pair, both small Cheshire towns, consistent with this file's existing small-group precedent (Wallop's 3-site Knutsford/Prestwich/Didsbury pattern, Cibo/Heddy's/Caramello). No evidence of a footprint beyond these two sites. Passes Hard rule 1. Coordinates from doogal.co.uk's postcode geocode for CW5 5NA. Reuses the existing BISTRO type (Residence Restaurant & Bar, Chestergate Bistro). Second addition to Nantwich this run — takes it from 5 to 7 venues, still the thinnest district in this file even after both additions.

suggestions.name: Rose & Crown
suggestions.reason: Three hundred and fifty years on King Street and still run as a proper coaching inn — nine rooms upstairs, a terrace out back, and Sunday lunch that doesn't need a gimmick.
suggestions.researchNotes: Verified via CAMRA (camra.org.uk), the inn's own site (knutsfordroseandcrown.co.uk) and Taste Cheshire: Rose & Crown Inn, 62 King Street, Knutsford WA16 6DT, a Grade-II-listed 1647 coaching inn — pub, restaurant and 9-room hotel, explicitly described by its own coverage as 'totally independent'. Single site, no group ownership found anywhere. Passes Hard rule 1 cleanly. Coordinates from a direct Apple Maps listing for the venue's own address. Reuses the existing GASTROPUB type (Wilmslow Tavern, HARCOURT, The Creameries) over COUNTRY PUB, since this is a town-centre coaching inn rather than a rural pub. Knutsford was at 9 venues (3 Do, 3 Drink, 3 Eat, already balanced) before this addition — simply adds to a balanced district's overall count.

suggestions.name: Rustik
suggestions.reason: Burton Road's own Irish corner — brunch by day, a proper session by night, family-run without a single chain tell in the fit-out.
suggestions.researchNotes: Verified via the venue's own site (rustikcafebar.co.uk), Yelp and manchestersfinest.com: Rustik, 198 Burton Road, West Didsbury, Manchester M20 1LH, an independent, family-run Irish neighbourhood bar/eatery — brunch by day, live music and a bar programme in the evenings. No second site or group ownership found anywhere. Passes Hard rule 1 cleanly. Coordinates from doogal.co.uk's postcode geocode for M20 1LH. Introduces a new venue type, IRISH BAR — no existing type/tile precisely fits a venue built around Irish-bar identity specifically rather than a general gastropub; left category-only (Drink), same precedent as ALE HOUSE/FRENCH BISTRO elsewhere in this file, not mapped to any onboarding tile yet. Didsbury was at 9 venues (3 Do, 3 Drink, 3 Eat, already balanced) before this addition — simply adds to a balanced district's overall count.
